tables.how: Every purchase-order number in the Controller's Purchase Order Summary, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date, for department ADM (City Administrator), the four suppliers by their exact names in the file, and a purchasing rule beginning 'Prop Q': 1,010 order numbers, 993 of them under 'Prop Q authority not bid' and the rest under 'Prop Q authority with bid'. The file has a row for each account line and fiscal year of an order; they are added up. For Rolling Stock Inc, not-bid orders dated 28 April 2022 to 21 October 2025 number 301 (in 272 orders, read from the first ten digits) and were paid $3,056,815.07. The limit was $10,000 through 30 June 2024 and $20,000 from 1 July 2024. 'Within 10 percent under the limit' marks the orders this site's screen counts (paid total from $9,000 to $10,000, or from $18,000 to $20,000 once payments are filed under fiscal 2025 or later, read from a pull of orders of $2,500 to $25,000). Counted from the full file the same rule gives 15, 86, 88 and 41 for Rolling Stock in fiscal 2022 to 2025, where the screen has 15, 85, 86 and 41.
tables.limits: The file shows orders and what was paid on them, not invoices: it cannot show whether several orders paid one invoice, which is what order splitting means. Tires, parts and repairs are bought vehicle by vehicle, and an order can be a small standing account drawn down by many invoices.  the rule forbids dividing one purchase to stay under it. No authority has examined these purchases. Orders under the later name 'Rolling Stock: Powered by Big Brand Tire' are not in this list.

tables.how: Purchase orders whose purchasing rule begins 'Prop Q', dated 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2024, with payments filed under fiscal 2021 to 2026 added up for each department and order number; orders with nothing paid are left out. That gives 74,370 orders, of which 4,521 (6.1%) were paid from $9,500 to $10,000. By department, among those with 100 or more orders: Human Resources 21.8% (104 of 478); Police 18.8% (402 of 2,137); Human Rights Commission 14.7% (73 of 495); City Administrator 14.0% (977 of 6,962); Airport Commission 11.3% (209 of 1,852); Fire Department 10.5% (194 of 1,852); Human Services Agency 7.4% (116 of 1,564); Sheriff 7.1% (207 of 2,902); Recreation & Park Commission 5.9% (730 of 12,433); Public Defender 5.1% (7 of 136); City Attorney 4.9% (6 of 122); Public Library 4.9% (59 of 1,212).
tables.limits: The file shows orders and what was paid on them, not invoices: it cannot show whether several orders paid one invoice, which is what order splitting means. Tires, parts and repairs are bought vehicle by vehicle, and an order can be a small standing account drawn down by many invoices.  the rule forbids dividing one purchase to stay under it. A department that buys many items priced near $10,000 will show a high share without splitting anything. 30 orders went to suppliers whose name reads as a private person's; those names are withheld and the order number identifies the record.
